title: החסילון שמרתיח את הים באגרוף אחד
summary: Pistol shrimp: WWII navies traced an underwater crackle that disturbed listening to shrimp beds; Versluis, Schmitz, von der Heydt & Lohse (Science 2000, 40,500 fps + hydrophone) showed the bang comes ~0.7 ms after the claw closes, from a collapsing cavitation bubble, not the claw; jet ~25 m/s; Bernoulli Δp = ½ρv² ≈ 3.1 atm (water tears near 14 m/s in the simple model); energy stored slowly behind a latch, released at once; Lohse 2001 faint flash, inferred >5,000 K ≈ 4,700 °C (near, not above, the Sun's surface); goby–Alpheus partnership in the Red Sea (Karplus 1974), Steinitz; maths: m/s → km/h ×3.6, distance = speed × time, ms to s, squares.
